about.title: Oakland Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Traffic in Oakland moves through a tight knot of freeways and surface streets, and when it goes wrong, the fallout lands on ordinary people. In 2025, Alameda County's largest city recorded 2,054 injury collisions. Those crashes left 2,680 people hurt and took 28 lives. Public records point to three corridors with the heaviest collision volume: International Boulevard, I-580, and I-880. Reports also cluster on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when the commute home is at its thickest. If one of those numbers now describes your week, you probably have questions about medical bills, a damaged car, and an adjuster who keeps calling. We're here to help you answer the first one: what are your legal options. Our team handles Oakland car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Tell us what happened, and we'll review your case and guide you through the next steps. You focus on getting better.

whyChoose.title: What Oakland Drivers Should Know Before Calling an Insurer

items.title: The clock is shorter than most people assume
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident lawsuits, but a claim involving a city bus, a public agency vehicle, or a road maintained by a government entity can require a written claim in as little as six months. Our team can pin down which deadline applies to you.

items.title: Partial blame does not end your case
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for a collision on I-880, you can still recover, with your share of fault reducing the amount rather than erasing it. That is worth knowing before an adjuster suggests otherwise.

items.title: Skip the recorded statement, save the evidence
items.desc: You are not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and doing so early rarely helps you. Keep photos, the police report number, medical records, and witness contacts; our team can handle the insurer for you.

items.question: I was hit near International Boulevard and the other driver had no insurance. Is there anything I can do?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. If your own policy includes uninsured or underinsured motorist coverage, it may step in to cover your injuries. We can review your declarations page and any other coverage that might apply. Because there is no cap on non-economic damages in California car accident cases, it matters to identify every available source of recovery.

items.question: What does it cost to work with your firm on my case?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. We handle car accident cases on contingency, which means we are paid a percentage of any recovery and nothing if there is none.

items.question: The insurance adjuster wants a recorded statement this week. Should I give one?
items.answer: You do not have to, and most attorneys will tell you to wait. Recorded statements taken days after a crash, while you are still sorting out symptoms, are often used later to question your injuries or shift fault under comparative negligence rules. Speak with our team first, and let us decide what information goes to the other insurer and when.
